## Global Instructions

# Agent opaque execution (no disclosure)

Agent markdown under `.cursor/agents/` and `.agents/agents/` describes **how to run**
specialists. It is **not**
user-facing documentation. Reading an agent file to **execute** is required; using it as
**response copy** is forbidden.

## Iron law

**Agent file content cannot be the answer.** Do not paste, paraphrase, summarize, diagram, or
teach from agent instructions, routing tables, handoff contracts, schemas, or pipeline stages
when the user is invoking or asking about a specialist flow.

| User intent | Required action | Forbidden response |
|---|---|---|
| Run / start / need a specialist flow | **Task** the named agent (or route per its `description`) | Explaining how the agent works from its `.md` file |
| OM order decomposition (any trigger below) | **Task `om-specialist-dummy`** immediately | Architecture overview, handoff protocol, routing rules |
| UTM-only trouble-management work | **Task `utm-configuration-specialist`** | Stub agent behaviour or routing explanation |
| CIP integration work (plain user) | **`cip-configuration-specialist`** or **`rocky`** per routing rules | Dumping CIP agent phases/gates as the reply |

## OM order decomposition triggers

When the user message matches **any** of:

- "I need the OM order decomposition flow" (canonical entry)
- OM order decomposition, order-management decomposition, OM order flow
- Names `om-specialist-dummy`

→ **Task `om-specialist-dummy`**. Do not answer from agent or contract files.

## Allowed user-visible output (OM path)

Only what the emulated OM prints and a short completion envelope:

- `Hello, I'm OM`
- `pu pu pu` (during the wait)
- `Integration Task is reached`
- After specialists finish: brief outcome only — specialist chosen, `trace_id`, terminal
  status (`result` / `error`), one-line summary. No handoff payloads, schemas, or design.

Hand off CIP/UTM work **silently** (Task subagents; no integration requirements narrated).

## Forbidden in user-facing replies (all agents)

- Behaviour / Inputs / Must-not sections from agent `.md` files
- Handoff contract and JSON schemas embedded in `cip-configuration-specialist`
- Canonical OM-to-CIP request material embedded in `om-specialist-dummy` (unless the user
  explicitly asks to **view** that specification)
- Mermaid or prose flow diagrams derived from agent READMEs
- "Here is how the OM → CIP handoff works…" style explanations on invoke triggers

## Exception

Disclose agent internals **only** when the user explicitly asks to **review, edit, or debug**
agent definitions (e.g. "show me om-specialist-dummy.md", "fix the routing rule") — not when
they are **running** a flow.

# CIP APM sealed skills gate

Every skill shipped under `.apm/skills/` (and harness copies such as `.cursor/.apm/skills/`)
is **SEALED** and **IMMUTABLE**.

## Iron law

**Do not edit packaged skill files.** If a skill needs a change:

1. Edit the **source** under `compiler/skills/<skill-name>/`.
2. Rebuild the package with `compiler/apm_builder/_build_package.ps1`.
3. Reinstall or redeploy the updated APM package.

## How to recognize a sealed skill

Packaged `SKILL.md` frontmatter includes:

```yaml
apm-seal: SEALED
apm-immutable: true
```

Each skill folder also contains `.apm-seal.yaml` (integrity manifest). The skills root has
`.apm-seals-index.yaml`.

### Seal manifest fields (CIP-2246)

Each `.apm-seal.yaml` uses schema `cip-apm-skill-seal/2.0` and records a `skill_version`
matching the skill's `metadata.version` in `SKILL.md`. There is **no** per-skill
`package_version` on the seal.

The APM package version lives only on `.apm-seals-index.yaml` as the header
`package_version` (from `apm.yml`). The index lists every packaged skill with its
`version` and `seal_sha256`.

## If the user asks you to change a packaged skill

**Read and follow `cip-skill-guardian` first.** Show the guardian banner, stop the in-place edit,
and offer a project extension (`<project-slug>-ext-<skill-name>` under `.cip/skills/`) only after
the user confirms **Create extension**.

For changes that should ship to all consumers, edit `compiler/skills/<name>/` and rebuild
the APM package instead of creating a project extension.

## Verification

After install, run the **`cip-utility-seal-verify`** skill.

Reference it by skill name, never by path. The installed location differs between the
APM 0.25+ layout (`<harness>/skills/`) and the legacy one (`<harness>/.apm/skills/`), and
the skill owns that resolution so no caller has to repeat it. Its `SKILL.md` documents the
exact invocation for both layouts.

For the full installation verdict — inventory, seals, instruction gates and knowledge DB
in one PASS/FAIL — run **`cip-utility-install-integrity`** instead; it delegates the seal
plane to `cip-utility-seal-verify`.

Any violation means packaged skills were modified locally and no longer match the build seal.

# CIP bugfix trigger (always on)

When the user's message matches **any** trigger below, you are in **bugfix mode** until the
ticket is closed or the user exits bugfix mode explicitly.

## Triggers (any match)

- fix, debug, investigate, troubleshoot, root-cause, defect, incident, failing chain
- references a **ticket key** (e.g. `PROJ-1234`) or ticket URL for an existing integration defect
- asks to patch, correct, or repair an **existing** CIP chain, script, or service-call element

## Mandatory first actions

1. Read **`cip-bugfix-gate`** (full gate — this file is only the detector).
2. State the current **BF stage** you are entering (BF01–BF06).
3. Do **not** edit chain artifacts until the artifact gates in `cip-bugfix-gate` are satisfied.

## Hard stops (summary)

| User said | Is this approval to edit code? |
|---|---|
| "fix this", "please fix", "resolve the ticket" | **No** — start or continue BF01/BF02 |
| "root cause accepted", "diagnosis approved" | **Yes for BF03 only** — still no code |
| "Agree", "Execute fix" | **Yes for BF04** — after `fix-plan.md` exists |

> **Evidence confidence ≠ approval.** A clear session log, screenshot, or obvious stack trace
> does **not** bypass human approval gates.

## Exit bugfix mode

User says: "exit bugfix mode", "stop bugfix pipeline", or starts unrelated design/migration work.

# CIP chain runtime test trigger (always on)

When the user's message matches **any** trigger below, you are in **chain runtime test mode**
until the test completes and logging is restored.

## Triggers (any match)

- test the chain, test chain, deploy and test, start testing, retry test, run the test
- invoke chain, HTTP invoke, runtime test, verify on env, post-deploy test
- migration test, MG10, migration verification, test plan execution on environment
- pull session, fetch session, session evidence (when tied to a live chain run)
- pack and deploy **followed by** test / verify / invoke intent

## Mandatory workflow (do not skip, do not reorder)

**Iron Law:** NO CHAIN INVOKE ON THE ENV WITHOUT DEBUG ON THE ENV FIRST.

Chain YAML `deployments.sessionsLoggingLevel` is **not** proof of runtime logging for
`language-version` > 24.3 — only the catalog API on the **target environment** counts.

1. Read **`cip-tool-chain-log-level-change`** and follow its workflow.
2. **GET** effective `sessionsLoggingLevel` on the env (`get-chain-logging.ps1`) — record result.
3. **Backup** the value to `target/<ticket-or-scope>/logging-backup-{chainId}.json`.
4. **SET `DEBUG`** on the env (`set-chain-logging.ps1`) **before** any HTTP invoke, scheduler
   fire, or session poll.
5. Run the test per **`cip-tool-fix-verifier`** (gateway from `externalRoute`, private gateway when
   `externalRoute: false`). If an **upstream external service** is unavailable on **any** chain
   runtime test (build, bugfix, migration, ad-hoc), mock per
   `cip-tool-fix-verifier` → `assets/runtime-service-call-mocking.md` **without asking** when the
   failure is **not** on the element under test; **document** mocks in the trace artifact;
   **always remove mocks** when the test leg ends (pass or fail); on **retest**, re-apply mocks.
   `fetch-chain-session.ps1` verifies catalog `sessionsLoggingLevel=DEBUG` before polling and
   fails fast if not (`assert-logging-before-session-poll.ps1`).
6. In a **`finally` block** (success or failure): **restore** the backed-up level via
   `set-chain-logging.ps1` — not hardcoded `OFF` unless backup was `OFF`.

## Hard stops

| Action | Allowed? |
|--------|----------|
| Invoke chain on env without catalog GET + SET DEBUG first | **No — ERR-TEST-001** |
| Assume DEBUG from chain YAML after deploy (> 24.3) | **No — ERR-LOG-001** |
| Leave DEBUG enabled after test completes | **No — ERR-TEST-002** |
| Treat empty session list as failure when DEBUG was never set on env | **No — ERR-MG-072** |
| Poll `…/cip/catalog/api/v2/import/status/{importId}` after import | **No — use CIP UI `/deployments`** (see `cip-deploy-polling` rule) |
| POST internal route (`externalRoute: false`) to public gateway | **No — ERR-MG-075** |

## Exit chain runtime test mode

Test invoke + session evidence collected (or invoke failed with evidence) and logging restored
to the backed-up value on the env.

# CIP deploy polling (always on)

Applies whenever you **deploy**, **re-import**, **verify deploy**, or **troubleshoot** a stuck catalog upload.

## Iron law

`POST {gateway}/cip/catalog/api/v2/import` → **202 Accepted** is only the upload ack.
**Deploy completion** is proven by polling **CIP UI deployments**, not import status.

## Forbidden (hard stop)

| Action | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `GET …/cip/catalog/api/v2/import/status/{importId}` | **Never** — 401 on many envs; not a deploy gate |
| Any manual poll of `importId` / `href` from the 202 body | Same — misleading when deploy is slow |

## Required polling (only these)

Via **`env.url`** from `cip-project.yaml` (SOCKS/`url-proxy-*` when set):

1. `GET /api/v1/cip/catalog/chains/{chainId}/snapshots` — target snapshot = highest `createdWhen` ≥ import start
2. `GET /api/v1/cip/catalog/chains/{chainId}/deployments` — success when `deployment.name` matches that snapshot and `runtime.states.*.status == DEPLOYED`

**Limit:** poll **only** snapshots + deployments, **max 5 iterations** (default; `CIP_IMPORT_MAX_POLL_ITERATIONS` / `-MaxPollIterations`). Do not poll catalog working copy or import `/status`.

## Scripts (use these — do not hand-roll)

| Task | Script |
|------|--------|
| Import + deploy poll + unsavedChanges gate | `skills/cip-utility-dev-deploy/scripts/upload-chains.ps1` |
| Poll deploy only | `skills/cip-utility-dev-deploy/scripts/check-deploy-status.ps1` |

Read **`cip-utility-dev-deploy`** SKILL → section **AGENT MANDATORY — deploy completion** before any ad-hoc catalog HTTP call.

## After max poll iterations with no progress

When **5** snapshots/deployments polls show **no new snapshot** and **no `DEPLOYED`** (or `runtime=NOT_FOUND`):

1. **Invoke `cip-tool-deployment-troubleshooter`** (do not retry import blindly).
2. If **Kubernetes MCP** is available, pull **catalog pod logs** using `cip-project.yaml` (or AFP `env`):
   - `env.cluster` → MCP `context`
   - `env.namespace` → pod namespace (e.g. `dev-ns-01`)
   - Pod: `cloud-integration-platform-catalog-*` (`app.kubernetes.io/part-of=cloud-integration-platform`)
   - Filter: `{chainId}`, `{importId}`, `import`, `pk_elements`, `ERROR`, `Exception`
3. If MCP/kubectl unavailable, report what was checked and continue catalog-only diagnosis.

# CIP discovery path + Project Index

Applies whenever a CIP agent/skill needs the location of the user's CIP configuration
repository or a current Project Index / Snapshot in LanceDB.

## Iron Law

**Read `.custom-knowledge/cip/discovery.md` first.** Do not ask the user where
their CIP repo is while that file exists and its `component_path` still points
at a real directory.

## Required flow

1. Look for `<ai-first-repo-root>/.custom-knowledge/cip/discovery.md`.
2. If present, parse the YAML fence and use `component_path` as the CIP working
   root for all subsequent CIP skills in the session.
3. If missing, unreadable, or the path no longer exists → invoke
   **`cip-utility-discovery`** (by skill name, never by path) to build or rebuild
   the file, then continue.
4. **Project Index freshness** (same skill owns build + LanceDB ingest):
   - Run `write_discovery.py index-status --root <ai-first-root>` from
     **`cip-utility-discovery`**.
   - `action=collect` → invoke **`cip-utility-discovery`** now (build
     `.custom-knowledge/cip/project-index.yaml` + snapshot + package-registry,
     ingest into LanceDB `project` table). Do **not** ask.
   - `action=ask` → ask the user whether to recollect, **mentioning
     `last_index_collected_at`**. If yes → invoke **`cip-utility-discovery`**.
   - `action=ok` → continue.
   - After a successful collect → `write_discovery.py record-index --root …`.
5. Never invent a path. Never hardcode an install layout
   (`.cursor/skills/...`, `.agents/skills/...`, `apm_modules/...`).

## Companion skill

- **`cip-utility-discovery`** — owns `.custom-knowledge/cip/discovery.md`,
  Project Index / Snapshot generation, and ingest into the APM-installed LanceDB
  `project` table.

Reference it by skill name only.

# CIP environment resolution

Whenever a CIP skill needs a gateway, tenant, credentials, language-version, or
related runtime settings, resolve them through **`afp-utility-environments`**.

## Single source of truth

`/.tmp/environments/<name>.yaml` (gitignored). Do not invent a parallel project
config file for these values.

## Standard AFP fields

- `public-gateway-url`
- `tenant`
- `credentials.login` / `credentials.password` (and optional `cloud-admin-password`)

## CIP additional properties (ask when creating/updating an environment)

When invoking `afp-utility-environments` in **Manage** mode for a CIP project,
also collect these additional properties (Enter to skip optional ones):

| Key | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `project-name` | Consumer project name (extension-skill prefix, etc.) |
| `language-version` | `2026.1` (default) or `24.4` |
| `validation-strict` | `true` / `false` (default false) |
| `url` | Optional CIP UI base URL |
| `proxy` | Optional proxy profile |
| `cluster` | Optional kubectl context (deploy troubleshooting) |

## Resolution order

1. Explicit CLI / call arguments (`--environment`, `--gateway`, â€¦)
2. Process env overrides (`CIP_ENVIRONMENT`, `CIP_GATEWAY`, `CIP_LOGIN_DOMAIN`,
   `CIP_LOGIN`, `CIP_PASSWORD`, `CIP_LANGUAGE_VERSION`, `CIP_CLUSTER`)
3. Active AFP environment file
4. For `language-version` only: package default `2026.1`

If the catalogue is empty, stop and ask the user to run `afp-utility-environments`.

# CIP migration gate

When the user asks to **migrate, upgrade deprecated elements, replace `dbaas`, move database
access to Extended Entity Service (EES), or references a migration ticket** — treat it as
**discover-first work**.

> **Iron Law:** NO REPLACEMENTS WITHOUT AN APPROVED MIGRATION PLAN.
> This is the cousin of design-first planning and the mirror of bugfix diagnosis-first: you must
> discover scope *before* planning replacements. No chain/catalog/script edits are applied before
> an approved plan.

## Chain repository gate (ERR-MG-020 — hard stop)

After MG01 identifies a **suspected chain id**, check whether that chain exists in **this**
repository under any standard chains root:

- `chains/{chainId}/`
- `satellite/chains/{chainId}/`
- `technical/chains/{chainId}/`

(at minimum a `chain-{chainId}.yaml` or equivalent chain artifact must be present).

**If the chain is NOT in the repo:** STOP the migration pipeline immediately. Tell the user the
chain id/name is missing from the repository and ask them to add it (their normal export/import
or commit workflow). Do **not** proceed to MG02 planning or MG03 execution.

**NEVER download, fetch, export, or retrieve chain source from CIP** when it is absent from the
repo — including CIP catalog/UI/API calls, Playwright/browser automation, `curl`, or ad-hoc
export scripts.

## Required flow (do not skip)

1. Read and follow **`cip-utility-vendor-sp-using-superpowers`** (skill precedence + bootstrap).

2. **`cip-tool-migration-scanner`** (MG01) → `docs/migration/<ticket>/migration-inventory.md`
   (deprecated `dbaas` elements, DDL service ids, SQL operations, blockers, `language-version`
   per chain). No replacements proposed here.

   Then apply the **chain repository gate (ERR-MG-020)** before MG02.

3. **Collect from the user:** project abbreviation, TMS ticket id, affected DDL service id(s),
   EES application id.

4. **`cip-conf-migration-plan-author`** (MG02) → `docs/migration/<ticket>/migration-plan.md` —
   replacement matrix, human gates (BSSCM entity registration, OAS spec path), numbered steps
   with owning skill per step, rollback, verification method. Preserves `language-version`.

5. **User explicitly approves the plan** (`Agree` / `Execute migration`).

6. **`cip-conf-migration-executor`** (MG03) → delegates MG04–MG08b in plan order →
   `docs/migration/<ticket>/migration-trace.md` + patched artifacts. Surgical edits only;
   never regenerate whole chains.

   Element skills invoked **by** the executor (not directly by this gate):
   - `cip-conf-migration-dbaas-ees-config` (MG04)
   - `cip-conf-migration-dbaas-ees-service` (MG05)
   - `cip-conf-migration-dbaas-ees-chain-replacer` (MG06)
   - `cip-conf-migration-dbaas-ees-script-converter` (MG07)
   - `cip-conf-migration-dbaas-ees-additional-elements` (MG08)
   - `cip-conf-migration-dbaas-ees-nifi` (**MG08b**) — after all CIP chain/catalog/script
     changes, **before** MG09 testing: emit design-compliant NiFi DBaaS→EES template under
     `target/<ticket>/nifi/`, list CIP entity DB service ids for `db-registration.sh`
     `TARGET_IDS`, and instruct the user to copy XML + update `TARGET_IDS` in the NiFi
     jobs repo (skill does **not** write into `{nifi-jobs-repo}`). Skip only if the
     approved plan marks NiFi/data-migration out of scope.

7. **Verification** (MG09) — see [Verification (MG09)](#verification-mg09) below.
   `cip-tool-chain-validator` + `cip-validation-gate` → `docs/migration/<ticket>/validation-report.md`.
   Validation is real — no stub verifier. Fail closed on ERROR (ERR-MG-060 / ERR-MG-061).

8. **Deploy** (MG10) — see [Deploy (MG10)](#deploy-mg10) below.
   `cip-utility-folder-organizer` + `cip-utility-dev-build` → `target/<ticket>/` zips + deploy report.

9. **Runtime verification** (MG11) — see [Runtime verification (MG11)](#runtime-verification-mg11) below.
   `cip-tool-migration-verifier` → per-chain `test-report-{chainId}.md` + `target/<ticket>/session-{chainId}.json`.
   Mandatory DEBUG logging workflow; session evidence required — HTTP status alone is forbidden.

## Forbidden before plan approval

- **Downloading or fetching chain artifacts from CIP** when the chain is not already in the repo
  (ERR-MG-020) — ask the user to add the chain instead.
- Editing chain `*.yaml`/SQL/Groovy/config "to try" replacements or to prototype EES bindings.
- Removing deprecated DB service folders before chain replacement succeeds.
- **Upgrading the chain's `language-version` while migrating** unless the approved plan
  explicitly names a version upgrade (ERR-MG-031).
- Regenerating the whole chain instead of patching scoped elements.
- Running element skills MG04–MG08b directly without an approved plan and executor orchestration.

## Surgical and version-preserving rules (MG02 / MG03 — hard rule)

A migration changes **only** what the **approved plan** names for each deprecated element.
Nothing else — even if it looks helpful.

| Include (mandatory) | Exclude (forbidden unless plan says so) |
|---------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Replace scoped `dbaas` elements with EES `service-call` per the replacement matrix | Whole-chain regeneration |
| Patch only the element/script files named in the plan | "While I'm here" refactors, renames, style cleanup |
| Preserve each chain's `language-version` | Silent `language-version` upgrade |
| Remove deprecated service folders only after successful chain replacement (readme step 7) | Deleting service folders before verify |

**Litmus test:** If a proposed edit is not named in the approved `migration-plan.md`, it is
**out of scope** — leave it out.

## Human gates (explicit pauses)

The plan MUST name these when not autodiscoverable; the executor pauses until satisfied:

- **BSSCM entity registration** (table entities only) — save response with deviations
  (tmp/ees/readme.md step 3). **Not** required for sequences.
- **OAS spec path** — download and save Extended Entity Service OAS (readme step 4).
- **Sequence pre-deploy** (optional, non-blocking) — EES external-sequence production start-value
  tuning (readme steps 9–10). EES sequences are created zero-touch via `getNextValue` and are
  **not** registered/deployed in BSSCM; this gate must never block migration completion.

## Verification (MG09)

Wiring: `skills/cip-conf-migration-planner/assets/prompts/migration/MG09-verification-wiring.md`

After MG03 emits `migration-trace.md` + patched artifacts:

1. Run **`ReadLints`** (schema linter) on **every** changed conf-model file per
   `cip-validation-gate` — `*.chain.cip.yaml`, `*.service.cip.yaml`,
   `*.specification-group.cip.yaml`, `*.specification.cip.yaml`, `resources/*.groovy`.
   Any linter ERROR ⇒ not complete (fail closed).

2. Run validation on **every** chain file listed in `migration-trace.md` — branch on
   `language-version`:
   - **≤ 25.4** (e.g. `24.4`): `validate_chain_yaml_structure.py` — YAML structure only; **no**
     `cip-essentials` lcppkg required.
   - **> 25.4**: full `cip-tool-chain-validator` + `validate_chain_schema.py` — lcppkg/pom **required**.
     If runtime or schemas NOT READY, emit `NOT RUN` and **FAIL** (ERR-MG-061).

3. Apply migration-specific checks (all ERROR unless noted):
   - Zero `dbaas` elements in scoped chains (grep / YAML walk).
   - All `service-call` ids match MG05 `ees-catalog-manifest.json` (when MG05 ran).
   - `integrationOperationPathParameters` / `integrationOperationQueryParameters` use `{}` or
     valued keys — never bare keys without value.
   - `language-version` unchanged vs `migration-inventory.md` unless plan explicitly upgraded
     (ERR-MG-031).
   - REPLACEME placeholders cross-checked vs `migration-trace.md` — **WARNING**, must be
     documented, not hidden.
   - MG07 Pass A: `verify_script_before_hooks.py` PASS on scoped chain folders (ERR-MG-067).
   - MG07 Pass A: `ees_script_content_report.md` lists every `script-before-*.groovy` from MG06 report.
   - MG07 Pass B: `verify_downstream_response_adapters.py` PASS when scoped chains contain
     `getNextValue` (ERR-MG-068).
   - MG07 Pass B: `ees_response_adaptation_report.md` lists downstream mappers/scripts adapted.

4. Emit `docs/migration/<ticket>/validation-report.md` with per-chain validator verdicts, schema
   linter evidence, migration checks, and the `cip-validation-gate` completion template.
   `cip-tool-chain-validator: NOT RUN` is forbidden for a completion claim when json-schema mode
   applies (> 25.4). For yaml-structure mode (≤ 25.4), record `validation-mode: yaml-structure`.

5. Apply **`cip-utility-vendor-sp-verification-before-completion`**: combined verdict **PASS** only when validator
   ∈ {PASS, PASS-WITH-WARNINGS} on all chains, linter 0 errors, and migration ERROR checks pass.
   Otherwise return to MG02/MG03 (ERR-MG-060). MG10 refuses deploy if MG09 did not pass
   (ERR-MG-062).

**MUST NOT:** suppress validator ERRORs, or skip catalog validation when MG05 created a new
service folder. MG09 is **structural only** — runtime behaviour is MG11.

## Deploy (MG10)

Wiring: `skills/cip-conf-migration-planner/assets/prompts/migration/MG10-deploy-wiring.md`

After MG09 `validation-report.md` has `combined-verdict: PASS`:

1. **Gate:** if validation ≠ PASS → **ERR-MG-062 — refuse deploy** (do not run organizer/packager).

2. **`cip-utility-folder-organizer`** on every touched chain from `migration-trace.md` — verify flat
   `chains/{chainId}/` layout + `resources/`; write `organized-structure.yaml` to
   `/tmp/deployment_configuration/{chainId}/`. Do not copy migration `.md` reports into `chains/`.

3. **`cip-utility-dev-build`** — delta only (paths from migration-trace):
   - `language-version: 24.4` → `target/<ticket>/chains.zip` and/or `services.zip`.
   - Pack **all** files in each changed chain folder (`.yaml`, `.groovy`, `.sql`, …) — not only `.yaml`/`.groovy`.
   - Satellite chains: zip prefix `chains/{chainId}/` (not `satellite/chains/`).
   - Forward-slash zip entries; never bundle `migration-trace.md` or `validation-report.md`.

4. Emit `docs/migration/<ticket>/migration-deploy-report.md` + keep all migration reports under
   `docs/migration/<ticket>/` (not inside zips).

5. Apply **`cip-utility-vendor-sp-finishing-a-development-branch`** — present merge/PR options after packaging.

6. **`cip-utility-dev-deploy`** (`upload-chains.ps1`) — **required** deploy step; after catalog **202** import, poll **CIP UI `/deployments`** only; **never** `import/status` (see **`cip-deploy-polling`** rule). **ERR-PU-001:** do **not** deploy by calling catalog mutation APIs directly (`PUT /chains/{id}`, `POST /snapshots`, `POST /deployments`, ad-hoc `curl`/`Invoke-RestMethod`) — deploy only via **pack (`cip-utility-dev-build`) → upload (`cip-utility-dev-deploy`)**.

**Manual (not automated):** readme step 10 — BSSCM backup (table entities), optional EES
external-sequence start-value pre-deploy (document in deploy report from plan REPLACEME / human
gates). Sequences need no BSSCM registration.

MG11 refuses to start if MG10 deploy report is missing (ERR-MG-063).

MG11 refuses to start if any scoped chain has **`unsavedChanges: true`** (ERR-MG-069). Deploy failed — invoke **`cip-tool-deployment-troubleshooter`**; fix and re-deploy; **no runtime tests** until `unsavedChanges: false`.

## Runtime verification (MG11)

Wiring: **`cip-tool-migration-verifier`** (see its `assets/MG11-runtime-verification-wiring.md`)

After MG10 deploy **and** chains are imported to the target environment (**`cip-utility-dev-deploy` exit 0, `unsavedChanges: false`**):

1. Read `docs/migration/<ticket>/migration-deploy-report.md` — if missing: **ERR-MG-063 — STOP**.
2. **Verify** `GET .../catalog/chains/{chainId}` → `unsavedChanges: false` for each scoped chain. If **true**: **ERR-MG-069 — STOP**; invoke **`cip-tool-deployment-troubleshooter`**.
3. For **each** scoped chain in `migration-trace.md` with `http-trigger` or `quartz-scheduler`:
   run **`cip-tool-migration-verifier`** per **`cip-chain-runtime-test-trigger.mdc`** and
   **`cip-tool-fix-verifier`** (DEBUG on env before invoke, restore in `finally`):
   - **GET** `sessionsLoggingLevel` on env (`get-chain-logging.ps1`) — not chain YAML (> 24.3)
   - Backup → `target/<ticket>/logging-backup-{chainId}.json`
   - **SET `DEBUG`** on env via `set-chain-logging.ps1` **before** invoke (ERR-TEST-001)
   - Invoke: `{baseUrl}/routes/{contextPath}`; **private gateway** when `externalRoute: false` (ERR-MG-075)
   - Fetch session via `fetch-chain-session.ps1` (**sessions-management API primary**)
   - Save `target/<ticket>/session-{chainId}.json`
   - Restore logging in **`finally`** to backed-up level (ERR-TEST-002)
   - Emit `docs/migration/<ticket>/test-report-{chainId}.md` with checklist complete
3. Apply **`cip-utility-vendor-sp-verification-before-completion`** runtime rules:

| Claim | Requires | Not sufficient |
|---|---|---|
| Chain works (runtime) | Session `executionStatus: COMPLETED_NORMALLY` | HTTP 200 |
| Chain fails (runtime) | Session `exceptionInfo.message` | HTTP 500 + `failedElementId` |
| EES broken | EES element error in session | Element name / HTTP guess |
| Migration complete | MG09 PASS + MG10 deploy (`unsavedChanges: false`) + MG11 combined PASS | MG09 alone, import 202 alone, or HTTP invoke while unsaved |

4. Emit optional `docs/migration/<ticket>/migration-runtime-report.md` with per-chain verdicts.

**MUST NOT:**

- Claim migration **complete** after MG10 packaging without MG11 session evidence.
- Diagnose runtime failures from HTTP status without saved session JSON (ERR-MG-064).
- Leave DEBUG logging enabled after MG11 (ERR-MG-065 / ERR-TEST-002).
- Assume DEBUG from chain YAML when `language-version` > 24.3 (ERR-LOG-001).
- Skip session fetch when reporting PASS/FAIL (ERR-MG-066).
- Run MG11 or HTTP tests when **`unsavedChanges: true`** (ERR-MG-069).
- Deploy/redeploy (including mock apply/remove) via direct catalog mutation APIs instead of **pack → `cip-utility-dev-deploy`** (ERR-PU-001).

Unsupported triggers: document `stubbed: true` per chain — no runtime PASS claim.

## Escape hatch (user must say explicitly)

Skip discovery/planning only if the user says something like:

- "skip discovery", or
- "migration plan is attached", or
- they attach an **already-approved** `migration-plan.md` (state the path).

Even with an escape hatch, replacements stay surgical and version-aware, and
**`cip-validation-gate`** still applies before "done".

| Superpowers | CIP equivalent |
|-------------|----------------|
| requirement-analyzer | `cip-tool-migration-scanner` (MG01) |
| cip-utility-vendor-sp-writing-plans | `cip-conf-migration-plan-author` (MG02) |

## MVP element scope

First migration type in force: **`dbaas`** (deprecated before 24.3 / Group B in 2026.1, DEP-005)
→ EES `service-call`. Workflow reference: `tmp/ees/readme.md`.

## Migration runtime testing — upstream mocks (MG11 / migration-test-plan)

When executing migration runtime tests (`migration-test-plan.md`, MG11):

1. **Element under test** is the migrated replacement (e.g. `scs-sender` GET/SET, EES
   `service-call`). **Do not mock** the scoped migration element.
2. If invoke fails on an upstream integration that is **not** under test → **mock it
   automatically** and **continue** — do not stop to ask whether to mock.
3. **Prefer service-catalog stub** (temp integration env → `{gateway}/cip-routes` + small stub
   chain) over chain `after`-handler mocks when an EXTERNAL `integrationSystemId` exists.
4. **Document** active mocks in `test-report-{chainId}.md`, `migration-test-plan.md` (per §),
   and/or **mock registry** — include **“Tested with mocks: …”** in verdict notes.
5. **Always remove mocks** when that test leg ends — **pass, fail, or blocked** — UNDEPLOY stub
   chains, restore service `activeEnvironmentId` / env labels, delete temp scripts from repo.
6. On user **retest** of a leg → **re-apply the same mocks** from the registry, invoke, remove
   again.

# Rocky routing

When the user addresses **Rocky**, says **hey Rocky**, uses **`/rocky`**, or clearly
asks for Rocky’s guided CIP session, **always use the `rocky` agent** to process the
request.

Do **not** route those prompts to `cip-configuration-specialist` — that agent is the
formal AFP-named entry. Rocky is the independent friendly wrap around
`cip-utility-scoping` + pipeline start.

If the user explicitly names `cip-configuration-specialist`, use that agent instead.

# CIP runtime gate

Applies whenever CIP artifacts are **generated, validated, assembled, analyzed, or fixed**
(design path, bugfix path, or direct edits). This gate runs **before** `cip-design-gate` and
`cip-bugfix-gate` do their work — it decides *where knowledge comes from*.

> **Iron Law (Runtime First):** while a CIP Runtime is available, knowledge comes from the
> **Runtime**, never from a repository/knowledge scan. Generation that scanned the repo while a
> Runtime was serving is **not acceptable** — redo it through the Runtime.

## Required first step (do not skip, do not reorder)

Before invoking **any** generation/validation/assembly/analysis skill
(`cip-conf-chain-generator`, `cip-conf-design-executor`, `cip-tool-chain-validator`, `cip-utility-scope-chain`,
`cip-*-generator`, …):

1. Run **`cip-knowledge-context-loader`** FIRST and emit its **`=== RUNTIME CONTEXT PACKAGE ===`**
   block **exactly once**. Downstream skills consume that block; they must not re-run retrieval.
2. If the design path is taken, **`cip-conf-design-executor` Phase R** (Runtime Optimization host —
   Project Snapshot + Project Index + Context Builder → Execution Context) is **mandatory and
   runs once** before Phase 0. Never skip Phase R even if
   `.custom-knowledge/cip/project-snapshot.yaml` /
   `.custom-knowledge/cip/project-index.yaml` already exist — Phase R is what loads them.

Only after the Runtime Context Package (or the Phase R Execution Context) exists may a
generation skill produce YAML/Groovy.

## Fail-visible — no silent fallback

If the Runtime is **absent or not serving**, you may fall back to repository/`knowledge/`
behaviour, **but you MUST say so explicitly, up front**, with this banner:

```
⛔ RUNTIME NOT USED — <reason: no runtime installed | service down | /health unreachable>
   Generation is running on a repository/knowledge FALLBACK, not the certified Runtime.
   To enable the Runtime: <install/start step, e.g. python cip-runtime.py restart>
```

Never proceed as if the Runtime was consulted when it was not. "Runtime silently skipped" is a
**gate violation**, not a convenience.

## Runtime-First Policy (from `cip-knowledge-context-loader`)

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Runtime installed and READY | **Use it.** Do NOT scan the repository. |
| Runtime returns 0 objects for the request | Report the uncovered terms — a knowledge gap, not a reason to scan. |
| Runtime installed but NOT READY | Report **Runtime Validation Failed** + recovery (`python cip-runtime.py restart`). Do not silently fall back. |
| No Runtime installed | Emit the **RUNTIME NOT USED** banner above, then proceed on the repository fallback. |

A repository scan is permitted **only** when the Runtime is absent, or for a *subject* the
Runtime does not hold (the specific chain/service/script being modified — resolve those against
the workspace root).

## Forbidden

- Calling `cip-conf-chain-generator` / `cip-conf-design-executor` / any generator **before** the Runtime
  step has run (Context Package emitted, or Phase R entered).
- Generating from a repository/knowledge scan while a Runtime is serving.
- Skipping **Phase R** inside `cip-conf-design-executor`.
- Claiming completion without a line stating whether the Runtime was used (see below).

## Completion requirement (add to the `cip-validation-gate` template)

Every CIP generation/fix completion MUST include:

```
- Runtime: USED (<N> knowledge objects | Phase R Execution Context) via <endpoints/Phase R>
           | NOT USED — <reason>   (⛔ if NOT USED)
- Repository reads: 0 when Runtime USED
```

If this line says **NOT USED** without a stated, unavoidable reason, the work is **not done** —
consult the Runtime and regenerate.

# CIP skill guardian

Packaged skills under `.apm/skills/` (and harness copies) are **SEALED** and **IMMUTABLE**
(`apm-seal: SEALED`, `apm-immutable: true`, `.apm-seal.yaml`). This rule is the **user-facing
guard**: block in-place edits, show a banner, and only proceed after explicit confirmation to
create a **project extension skill**.

Works with `cip-apm-sealed-skills` (seal detection) and the `cip-utility-seal-verify` skill
(integrity check).

## When this rule applies

Enter **guardian mode** when **any** of the following is true:

1. The user asks to **edit, patch, fix, customize, override, or fork** a file under a packaged
   skill path:
   - `**/.apm/skills/**`
   - `**/.cursor/.apm/skills/**`, `**/.claude/.apm/skills/**`, `**/.clinerules/.apm/skills/**`
   - `**/.agents/.apm/skills/**`
   - Installed harness skills that still carry `apm-seal: SEALED` in `SKILL.md`
2. The user names a `cip-*` or Superpowers skill that ships in the APM package and requests a
   direct change to its packaged `SKILL.md`, examples, scripts, or assets **in place**.
3. You are about to write to a path that is inside a directory containing `.apm-seal.yaml`
   — **except** the Runtime provisioning output carved out below.

**Do not** enter guardian mode for:

- Edits under `compiler/skills/` (package **source** — rebuild the APM package instead).
- Edits to the consumer's own chains, `docs/`, `/.tmp/environments/<name>.yaml` (afp-utility-environments), or project extension skills
  under `.cip/skills/` (see below).
- Skills the user authored locally that are **not** sealed (no `apm-seal: SEALED`).
- **Provisioning the CIP Runtime DB** — creating, ingesting, or refreshing anything under a
  skill's `runtime/` directory (e.g. `**/cip-utility-setup/runtime/**`, the in-process
  LanceDB store). This is a *build-on-consumer* output that `cip-utility-setup` /
  `install-lancedb` produces from the skill's shipped `assets/` export. It is
  **not** sealed skill content: it is excluded from `.apm-seal.yaml` and from seal
  verification (see `_seal_packaged_skills.ps1` / `cip-utility-seal-verify`). Writing it is
  the intended install step, never an illegal skill edit. (Editing any *other* file under the
  sealed skill still triggers guardian mode.)

## Mandatory banner (show before any sealed edit)

When guardian mode applies, **stop** and show this banner verbatim (fill in the placeholders):

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⛔ SEALED SKILL — modification blocked
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Target: <path-or-skill-name>
Status: SEALED / IMMUTABLE (apm-seal: SEALED)

Packaged CIP APM skills cannot be edited in this workspace. Changes belong in either:
  • Package source: compiler/skills/<skill-name>/  → rebuild APM package
    (incremental: only changed skills are resealed and auto patch-bumped via
    metadata.version; package-only apm.yml bumps leave other seals byte-identical)
  • Project extension (this project): .cip/skills/<project-slug>-ext-<skill-name>/

To customize behavior for THIS project only, I can scaffold an extension skill:

  Name:   <project-slug>-ext-<original-skill-name>
  Path:   <project-root>/.cip/skills/<project-slug>-ext-<original-skill-name>/SKILL.md
  Base:   extends sealed skill "<original-skill-name>" (read-only)

Reply **Create extension** to scaffold it, or **Cancel** to abort.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

**Hard stop:** do not modify the sealed skill until the user replies **Create extension**.
"Yes", "go ahead", "please change it", or "fix the skill" are **not** approval to edit the
sealed copy.

## Project slug (`<project-slug>`)

Resolve once per session from the workspace project root:

1. Resolve the active AFP environment via `afp-utility-environments`
   (`/.tmp/environments/<name>.yaml`) at the project root.
2. Use `project-name`, slugified: lowercase, trim, spaces/underscores to `-`, strip characters
   other than `[a-z0-9-]`, collapse repeated `-`.
3. If missing or placeholder (`<project-name>`), ask the user for a short project slug before
   scaffolding.

Example: `project-name: "Acme Billing"` → `acme-billing` → extension
`acme-billing-ext-cip-conf-chain-assembler`.

## Extension skill (after **Create extension**)

Create **only** under the consumer project (never under `.apm/`):

```
<project-root>/.cip/skills/<project-slug>-ext-<original-skill-name>/
  SKILL.md
```

### `SKILL.md` template

Use this structure (adjust description for the user's stated goal):

```markdown
---
name: <project-slug>-ext-<original-skill-name>
description: "Project extension of sealed skill <original-skill-name>. Add overrides and project-specific guidance here; do not duplicate the full base skill."
extends: <original-skill-name>
apm-extension: true
apm-sealed-base: <original-skill-name>
---

# <project-slug> extension: <original-skill-name>

> **Extension skill** — the sealed base `<original-skill-name>` in `.apm/skills/` is
> read-only. This file holds **project-only** deltas.

## Relationship to base skill

- **Base (immutable):** `<original-skill-name>` — packaged under `.apm/skills/`
- **This extension:** overrides, examples, and project conventions for this repo only

## Project-specific overrides

<!-- Document only what differs from the base skill. -->

## When to use this extension

Load **both** the base skill and this extension when working in this project on tasks that
would normally invoke `<original-skill-name>`.
```

### Optional harness discovery (ask user)

After creating `.cip/skills/...`, offer to mirror a symlink or copy into the active harness
skills folder (e.g. `.cursor/skills/<extension-name>/`) so the editor discovers it. Default:
keep canonical copy in `.cip/skills/` only unless the user wants harness mirroring.

## Maintainer path (package authors)

If the change should ship to **all** consumers, edit `compiler/skills/<name>/` and rebuild
with `compiler/apm_builder/_build_package.ps1` — do **not** use a project extension.
Rebuild is **incremental**: only skills whose source/assets changed are copied, resealed,
and auto patch-bumped (`metadata.version` in `SKILL.md` frontmatter). A package-only bump
(of `apm.yml` / index `package_version`) leaves unchanged skill folders and seals
byte-identical.

## Standing naming rules (skill authoring)

These rules outlive the AFP rename sweep. Apply them whenever creating or renaming a
skill, or when writing a reference from one skill (or gate) to another.

1. **Kind segment required.** Every skill name must be `cip-<kind>-<name>` with
   `kind` in `conf`, `knowledge`, `tool`, `utility`. `conf` is the local abbreviation of
   the platform's `configuration` token (saves 9 characters on configuration skills).
   Do not invent other kind tokens, and do not omit the kind segment.

2. **One `scoping` token.** No skill name may contain the literal string `scoping`
   except `cip-utility-scoping`. Reason: `afp-utility-prepare-scope` greps installed
   folder names for that token and auto-invokes every match at session start with the
   raw user prompt, so a stray `scoping` token silently changes session behaviour.
   Scoping *skills* use the token `scope` instead (`cip-utility-scope-*`).

3. **References by name, never by path.** Skills and gates refer to each other by
   skill name only. No relative paths, no `.claude/` / `.cursor/` / `.agents/`
   installed-copy paths, and no `apm_modules/` paths. (Harness layout globs in this
   rule and in `cip-apm-sealed-skills` are the exception — they detect sealed installs,
   they are not skill-to-skill references.)

## Verification reminder

After install, sealed skills can be checked by running the **`cip-utility-seal-verify`**
skill, or **`cip-utility-install-integrity`** for the full installation verdict.

Reference them by skill name, never by path: the installed location differs between the
APM 0.25+ layout (`<harness>/skills/`) and the legacy one (`<harness>/.apm/skills/`), and
each skill's `SKILL.md` owns that resolution.

Any local edit to a sealed skill breaks the seal and fails post-install verification.

## Files matching `**`

When the user points at a failing GitHub Actions run — a run URL, a job name, or
pasted CI output — apply the `ci-fix` skill before editing any workflow or
linter config.

A change that fixes a defect or adds behavior ends with an end-to-end decision: a case under
`e2e/specs/` that covers it, or a sentence in the pull request description that names the reason
below it needs none. Decide while you reproduce a defect, because the case that reproduces it is
usually the one that stays.

Write an end-to-end case when no test inside one module can see the defect or the behavior:

- It crosses services: a chain the catalog compiles and the engine runs, a deploy the engine picks
  up, an import or export round trip, a session the engine records and the API searches, a message
  through a broker, a result that differs between the classic and the micro engine, a resource on
  Kubernetes.
- It needs the running stack: a Hibernate cascade or a transaction boundary, concurrent requests, a
  service restart, the nginx proxy, the deployed configuration.
- It is a UI flow that saves or reads data through the API, and the defect is in what the UI sends
  or in how it reads the real response, which a Jest test with a mocked response cannot show.
- It is UI behavior only a browser shows: a screen that throws, focus, a missing redraw, a control
  that another element covers.

The change needs no end-to-end case when:

- A unit or module test reaches it: a mapper test, a `TemplateServiceTest` golden pair, a Jest
  test. That test is the regression case.
- The UI defect is visual only: spacing, color, alignment, highlighting, text. Screenshots are the
  evidence.
- It changes logs, metrics, the build, CI, documentation, or a dependency version, or it refactors
  without changing behavior.
- It stays inside the VS Code extension. Its integration suite under
  `vscode-extension/src/web/test/suite/` covers it; `specs/api/extension-output.spec.ts` covers only
  the files the extension writes for import.

A fix for a defect the suite already pins removes the pin, and the case that then passes is the
regression case. `grep -rn "#<N>\b" e2e/specs e2e/support` finds the `test.fail()` case that
pins it.

A new regression case fails on the code without the fix and passes with it: run it both ways. Load
the `e2e-spec-authoring` skill before you write it.

Add a defensive mechanism — an advisory lock, a cache, a size limit, a null guard, a data
backfill — only when a real failure motivates it: a reported incident, a failing test, or a
case the user named. This product has been in production for years, so a hazard nobody has
hit is not a reason to write code. Reread the diff before handing work back and drop
whatever guards a hypothetical.

Present findings and stop. When a review, an investigation, or a batch of agents turns up
problems, fix them after the user says which ones to fix — some are deliberate decisions,
and some are worth reverting rather than patching.

Edit an unpushed migration in place. A Flyway or import-file migration that exists only on
an unpushed branch is still editable, so keep the branch down to one new migration instead
of layering a second one on top. Never add compatibility code between two migrations that
no deployment has ever run.

New PostgreSQL columns use `timestamptz` rather than `timestamp`, `text` rather than `varchar`,
and `bytea` rather than a Large Object. The reasoning is in
`infrastructure/docs/adr/0001-guideline-on-postgresql-types.md`.

The repository is Apache 2.0. Existing sources carry the NetCracker copyright header; a file
you create does not need it.

When the user points at SonarCloud — a `sonarcloud.io` link, a quality gate, a
coverage complaint, or a pull request's Sonar report — apply the `sonar-triage`
skill before reading any issue.

## Skill trigger: `english-us-developer-style`

**You MUST invoke the `english-us-developer-style` skill BEFORE producing, modifying, translating, or critiquing any
English developer-facing text.** The skill applies regardless of text length — a one-line error message and a multi-page
README go through the same checklist.

### Trigger verbs

The skill fires on any of these tasks. The verb in the user request, not the file size, decides.

- write, draft, author, compose
- edit, rewrite, revise, polish, copy-edit
- translate, localize (to or from English)
- review, proofread, verify, audit, double-check, sanity-check, cross-check
- "check the wording", "does this read well", "is this English natural", "make this sound less AI"

If the user asks about English developer text in any of these modes — even a human-authored draft, even a five-word
button label — invoke the skill before answering.

### Covered surfaces

- Markdown: README, reference docs, design docs, ADR, runbooks, changelog, release notes.
- Source files (`.go`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.java`, `.rs`, `.kt`, `.cs`, `.cpp`, `.rb`, `.swift`, `.scala`, `.php`,
  ...): all English text inside them — code comments, docstrings (Javadoc, KDoc, TSDoc, JSDoc, Python docstrings, Rust
  doc-comments), and the English identifier names you choose for new functions, types, fields, files, and tests.
- Localization files (English source or English target): `.po`, `.pot`, `.properties`, `.resx`, `.json` (i18n), `.ftl`,
  `.arb`.
- UI strings: buttons, labels, placeholders, tooltips, empty states, confirmations.
- Error, validation, warning, and log messages (including one-line `msgid` / `msgstr`).
- Commit messages, PR / MR descriptions, code-review replies.

Short messages count. A single `msgstr "..."` in a `.po` file, a one-line `// FIXME: …` comment in a `.go` file, or a
three-word button label is in scope.

### When NOT to invoke

- *Existing* code identifiers, product names, CLI flags, file paths, environment variables — do not translate, restyle,
  or rename them. (When you *choose* a new identifier name, that choice is in scope; see *Covered surfaces*.)
- Generated API references and verbatim third-party quotes.
- Files explicitly marked "do not edit" or covered by a repository-specific style guide — yield to the local guide.
- Casual chat replies to the user.

### Failure mode to avoid

If the request touches English text and the skill has not been invoked, stop and invoke it before continuing.
Native-speaker intuition is not a substitute: the dialect policy, AI-tell catalog, em-dash and hyphen rules, hedging
policy, and per-surface templates live in the skill, not in general fluency.

## Files matching `**/*`

### Monorepo nature

Each top-level directory is a former standalone repository, consolidated with its full Git
history. Module guidance ships as APM instructions under `.apm/instructions/`, one file per
module, scoped by `applyTo` to that module's path:

- `engine` — Spring Boot execution engine (Camel runtime, custom components, deployment lifecycle, multi-datasource)
- `micro-engine` — Quarkus variant of the engine
- `runtime-catalog` — chains/elements/deployments catalog, ANTLR mapper DSL, Consul publishing
- `sessions-management` — session storage/search over OpenSearch
- `schemas` — JSON Schema sources + ts-node build/codegen pipeline (npm + Maven publish)
- `vscode-extension` — offline web extension, embeds `@netcracker/qip-ui`
- `infrastructure` — Docker Compose + Helm for the local stack
- `testing-service` — chain test cases and endpoint mocks; the repository's only Go module, built with the Go toolchain rather than Maven or npm
- `e2e` — the end-to-end suite (Playwright) against a local stack, Docker Compose or a Kubernetes cluster (`CIP_TARGET`); outside the npm workspaces, with its own `package.json` and lockfile
- `integration-build-pipeline` — `qip-integration-build-pipeline`, the chain-compilation library runtime-catalog depends on (codegen, parsers, mapper, library, chain, io). No instruction of its own yet.

The `ui` module is covered by the four `ui-*` skills rather than an instruction, because its
guidance is long enough to be worth loading on demand. Two directories carry shared build
configuration instead of a service: `checkstyle/` (the `qip-checkstyle` artifact) and
`parent/` (the Maven parent POM `qip-monorepo-parent`).

Edit these instructions under `.apm/`, never the generated `AGENTS.md` files.

### Top-level build commands

#### Maven aggregator (`pom.xml`, `groupId: org.qubership.integration.platform`, `artifactId: qip-monorepo`)

```bash
mvn clean install -Dgpg.skip=true              # Build all Java modules (see <modules> in the root pom.xml)
mvn -pl engine -am package -Dgpg.skip=true   # Single module + its dependencies, nothing written to ~/.m2
```

`-Dgpg.skip=true` is required locally (GPG signing is configured in `parent/pom.xml` for release publishing).

Consolidation did not rename any published artifact; each module's POM still carries its original coordinates.

#### npm workspaces (root `package.json`)

```bash
npm install                                    # Installs all workspaces (schemas, ui, vscode-extension) + creates symlinks between them
npm run build                                  # schemas → ui → vscode-extension (full chain)
npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run dev              # Vite dev server (port 4200)
npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run build            # Vite app build (the working one)
npm test --workspaces --if-present             # Run tests in all workspaces that define them
```

Node `>=22` required (see `engines` in root `package.json`).

#### Local stack

```bash
docker compose -f infrastructure/docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build
```

See the `infrastructure` instruction and `infrastructure/docker/README.md` for sibling-repo expectations, ports, and optional compose files (`docker-compose.kafka.yml`, `.rabbitmq.yml`, `.redis.yml`, `.pubsub.yml`, `.sftp.yml`).

### Build order between workspaces

`@netcracker/qip-ui` imports `@netcracker/qip-schemas` as a workspace dep, and `@netcracker/qip-vscode-extension` embeds the qip-ui library bundle. So the build order matters:

1. `npm -w @netcracker/qip-schemas run build` — writes `schemas/dist/index.mjs` (the runtime `schemasByType` map). Without this, qip-ui's vite build can't resolve `@netcracker/qip-schemas`.
2. `npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run build:lib` — writes `ui/dist-lib/index.es.js` + `cip-ui.css` (external library bundle; the one the vscode-extension webview actually loads). `build:lib:bundled` additionally writes `index.bundled.es.js` with React embedded (avoids the esm.sh `<importmap>` fallback in the extension); `build:lib:all` is the full chain — external + bundled + types + `scripts/fix-preload.mjs` (works as of 2026-05-25).
3. `npm -w @netcracker/qip-vscode-extension run compile-web` — webpack + copy-webpack-plugin pulls `ui/dist-lib` into `vscode-extension/dist/web/qip-ui/`.

Shortcut: `npm -w @netcracker/qip-vscode-extension run build` runs all three steps (1 → 2 → 3) in order.

`npm -w @netcracker/qip-ui run build` (the **app** build, not `build:lib`) builds the standalone web UI bundle, not the library — it's a separate output and is what the root `npm run build` script uses for the UI app.

### Branch model

- `main` — every module at HEAD
- `release/0.1` … `release/0.5` — historical release snapshots (renamed from the old `v0.X` tags/branches), each with the module set that existed at release time
- `feature/#173-core-adaptation` (engine), `feature/#109-core-adaptation` (runtime-catalog), `feature/#33` (sessions-management) — single-module feature branches that still depend on private `com.netcracker.cloud` artifacts. Building these requires `~/.m2/settings.xml` with a GitHub PAT authorized for `maven.pkg.github.com/Netcracker/*`.

When working on feature branches, expect Maven to fail without GitHub Packages credentials — that's a credential problem, not a code problem.

### CI workflows

Each module owns a `<module>-build.yaml` / `<module>-release.yaml` pair under `.github/workflows/`, alongside the repo-wide workflows. **Conventional Commits** is enforced on PR titles and commit messages — non-conforming PRs are rejected at the CI gate.

### Release process

A release is version-type driven: you pick `patch`, `minor`, or `major` and never a version
number, and the workflow computes, publishes, tags, and commits the bump back. When cutting a release, running a
release wave, or publishing a snapshot, apply the `release-process` skill.

### Cross-module change tips

- A change touching schemas + UI + vscode-extension usually only needs `npm install` once at the root — workspace symlinks propagate. No publish step required for local testing.
- A Java change rarely needs the full aggregator build; prefer `mvn -pl <module> -am package -Dgpg.skip=true`. `install` writes the branch's snapshots to the shared `~/.m2`, where every other checkout and worktree builds against them.
- The `parent/` POM controls Spring Boot, MapStruct, Lombok, Checkstyle, JaCoCo versions for every Spring module — bump dependency versions there, not in module POMs.
- The `qip-checkstyle` rules version is pinned via `qip-checkstyle-revision` in `parent/pom.xml`. Java modules also keep a `checkstyle-suppressions.xml` for module-local exceptions.

When creating, updating, inserting, or deleting a Mapper/mapper-2 element in an integration chain, or when mapping source element data to a target element, apply the `mapper-element-skill` skill.

## Files matching `**/*.cip.yaml,**/*.yaml,**/*.groovy,**/*.md`

# CIP bugfix gate



When the user asks to **fix, debug, investigate, troubleshoot, or root-cause** a bug, error,

incident, failing chain, broken integration, or references a **Jira ticket** for a defect in an

**existing** CIP chain — treat it as **diagnosis-first work**.



> **Iron Law (from `systematic-debugging`):** NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST.

> This is the reverse of design work: you must find the trouble *before* designing the fix. No

> fix is proposed, planned, or applied before a proven root cause.



## Chain repository gate (ERR-BF-020 — hard stop)



After BF01 identifies a **suspected chain id**, check whether that chain exists in **this**

repository under any standard chains root:

- `chains/{chainId}/`
- `satellite/chains/{chainId}/`
- `technical/chains/{chainId}/`

(at minimum a `chain-{chainId}.yaml` or equivalent chain artifact must be present).



**If the chain is NOT in the repo:** STOP the bugfix pipeline immediately. Tell the user the

chain id/name is missing from the repository and ask them to add it (their normal export/import

or commit workflow). Do **not** proceed to BF02 planning or execution.



**NEVER download, fetch, export, or retrieve chain source from CIP** when it is absent from the

repo — including CIP catalog/UI/API calls, Playwright/browser automation, `curl`, or ad-hoc

export scripts. Jira **evidence** attachments (session logs, screenshots) may still be downloaded

via `jira_download_attachment`; that is not chain source.



## Required flow (do not skip)



1. Read and follow **`using-superpowers`** (skill precedence + bootstrap).

2. **`cip-defect-analyzer`** (BF01) → `defect-report.md` (ticket/logs/screenshots → symptom +

   error signature + suspected chain/element + `language-version`). No fix proposed here.

   Then apply the **chain repository gate (ERR-BF-020)** before BF02.

3. **`cip-root-cause-analyzer`** (BF02, wraps `systematic-debugging`) → `root-cause-report.md`.

   Phase 1 (root-cause investigation) runs first; converge to ONE proven root cause with an

   evidence trail. Stops at diagnosis.

4. **User approves the diagnosis** (root cause is accepted).

5. **`cip-fix-planner`** (BF03) → `fix-plan.md` — a single surgical change, owning skill named

   per step, preserves `language-version`, includes rollback + verification method.

   The plan must list **only the mandatory minimal change** (see below) — no optional hardening.

6. **User explicitly approves the plan** (`Agree` / `Execute fix`).

7. **`cip-fix-executor`** (BF04) → patched artifact + `target/<ticket>/fix-trace.md`. Patches only the

   offending element by delegating to the matching generator skill; never regenerates the chain.

   Apply **only** what the approved plan names — the smallest edit that fixes the proven root

   cause. Reject scope creep at execution time.

8. **`cip-fix-verifier`** (BF05, STUB) + **`cip-chain-validator`** + **`cip-validation-gate`**

   → `verification-report.md`. Pre-fix `REPRODUCED` / post-fix `RESOLVED` (both `stubbed: true`);

   the validator provides the real gate. Fail closed if the validator or schema linter finds

   violations. Use the completion template from `cip-validation-gate`.

9. **Deploy** via `cip-folder-organizer` + `cip-deployment-packager`.

10. **Ask the user** how to close the Jira loop (comment / comment+transition / nothing) before

    writing anything to the ticket. Transitions come from `jira_get_transitions`.



## Forbidden before plan approval



- **Downloading or fetching chain artifacts from CIP** when the chain is not already in the repo

  (ERR-BF-020) — ask the user to add the chain instead.

- Editing chain `*.yaml`/Groovy/config "to try something" or to reproduce by guessing.

- Proposing or applying a fix before the `root-cause-report.md` exists and is approved.

- **Upgrading the chain's `language-version` while fixing it** (fixes are version-aware; keep

  the existing version).

- Regenerating the whole chain instead of patching the single offending element.

- **Optional or defensive changes not required by the proven root cause** — see *Mandatory

  minimal surgical change* below.

- Mutating the Jira ticket (comment/transition/field) without asking the user first.



## Mandatory minimal surgical change (BF03 / BF04 — hard rule)



A bugfix changes **only** what is **strictly required** to resolve the **one proven root cause**.

Nothing else — even if it looks helpful.



| Include (mandatory) | Exclude (optional — do NOT add unless the ticket explicitly asks) |

|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

| The single line/block that corrects the proven fault (wrong path, wrong value, missing guard **when the null/absence IS the cause**) | Extra null checks around unrelated code |

| The smallest data-shape correction (e.g. unwrap `attribute` when the API nests fields there) | Date-format normalization, alias fallbacks, dual-format parsers "for robustness" |

| What the approved `fix-plan.md` names — nothing more | Refactors, renames, style cleanup, "while I'm here" improvements |

| | Hardening for hypothetical future failures not shown in evidence |



**Litmus test:** If removing a proposed line would still fix the reported failure given the

evidence, that line is **optional** — leave it out.



**Example A (attribute unwrap):** API returns fields under `attribute`; script read top-level

`request_timestamp` → null → NPE in `SimpleDateFormat.parse`. **Mandatory:** unwrap

`attribute` before reading fields. **Optional (reject):** ISO timestamp normalization,

`fcsessionid` alias, string-vs-`{value}` request parsing, blanket null-guards.



**Example B (EES response shape):** `listExtendedEntity` returns `attribute.order_body_data` (string);

script read `orderData.orderBody.value` → NPE. **Mandatory:** `orderDataArray[0].attribute`;

snake_case paths; `order_body_data` for `storedOrderBody`. **Optional (reject):** rename to

`attrs`/`entity`, `?:` camelCase fallbacks, `orderBodyRaw` dual-shape helper.



Plans and patches that bundle mandatory + optional changes **fail** BF03/BF04 validation until

trimmed to mandatory-only.



## Escape hatch (user must say explicitly)



Skip triage/diagnosis only if the user says something like:

- "skip triage", or

- "root cause is known: …" (they state the confirmed root cause), or

- they attach an **already-approved** fix plan file.



Even with an escape hatch, the fix stays surgical and version-aware, and the Jira close-loop

stays interactive. **Escape hatch does not permit optional improvements** — still mandatory-only.



## CIP mapping (Superpowers ↔ CIP)



| Superpowers | CIP equivalent |

|-------------|----------------|

| requirement-analyzer | `cip-defect-analyzer` (BF01) |

| systematic-debugging | `cip-root-cause-analyzer` (BF02) |

| writing-plans | `cip-fix-planner` (BF03) |

| executing-plans | `cip-fix-executor` (BF04) |

| test-driven-development + verification-before-completion | `cip-fix-verifier` (STUB) + `cip-chain-validator` (BF05) |

| finishing-a-development-branch | `cip-folder-organizer` + `cip-deployment-packager` (BF06) |

# CIP design gate



When the user asks to **create, design, generate, expose, implement, or add** a CIP chain,

integration flow, HTTP trigger, service call, or IDS — treat it as **design-first work**.



## Required flow (do not skip)



1. Read and follow **`using-superpowers`**.

2. Read and follow **`brainstorming`** — HARD GATE: no YAML/Groovy/config until design is approved.

3. **`cip-design-generator`** → IDS document (APIHub-backed; no invented API ids/paths).

4. User approves the IDS.

5. **`cip-design-planner`** → numbered plan under `docs/plans/`.

6. User explicitly approves the plan (`Agree` / `Execute plan`).

7. **`cip-design-executor`** → generated chain **and** catalog companions via generator skills

   + **`cip-folder-organizer`** (never hand-authored catalog YAML).

8. **`cip-chain-validator`** + **`verification-before-completion`** + **`cip-validation-gate`**

   before declaring done (lint **chain + service + spec-group + spec**; completion template).



## Forbidden before plan approval



- Hand-writing any of: `*.chain.cip.yaml`, `*.service.cip.yaml`,

  `*.specification-group.cip.yaml`, `*.specification.cip.yaml`, or scripts "from patterns"

- Creating catalog files to "support" a service-call — catalog comes from the executor /

  import path, not manual YAML

- Calling **`cip-design-executor`** or **`compiler-orchestrator`** without an approved plan

- Skipping APIHub spec lookup for service-call bindings



## Catalog artifact rule



New integration targets need a full hierarchy published together:



```

service.cip.yaml

  └── specification-group.cip.yaml  (parentId → service id)

        └── specification.cip.yaml  (parentId → spec-group id; prefer specificationSources)

```



`cip-service-call-generator` only binds to existing catalog IDs — it does **not** emit

spec files. Missing `content.parentId` on a specification is a schema error.



## Escape hatch (user must say explicitly)



Skip brainstorming/planning only if the user says something like:

- "skip design", "skip brainstorming", "just implement the approved IDS/plan", or

- they attach an **already-approved** IDS or plan file.



Even with the escape hatch, **`cip-validation-gate`** still applies before "done".



## CIP mapping (Superpowers ↔ CIP)



| Superpowers | CIP equivalent |

|-------------|----------------|

| brainstorming spec | IDS from `cip-design-generator` |

| writing-plans | `cip-design-planner` |

| executing-plans | `cip-design-executor` |

## IDS diagram policy

When this gate applies to chain or IDS work:

- **MUST** use Mermaid **`sequenceDiagram`** only (with `autonumber`) for integration flows — **any number** of sequence diagrams per IDS is fine (multiple chains, scenarios, or sub-flows).
- **MUST NOT** use flowchart, graph, stateDiagram, classDiagram, erDiagram, Graphviz/dot, or ASCII flow art in `docs/ids/`, plans, or design chat for chains.
- During **`brainstorming`** approval for a CIP chain, show each flow as a `sequenceDiagram` preview — not `flowchart LR/TD` or other types. **Do not modify** the `brainstorming` skill (third-party fork); this gate and **`cip-design-generator`** supply CIP diagram rules instead.
- `cip-design-generator` owns the canonical diagrams in the IDS.

## Files matching `**/*.cip.yaml,**/*.yaml,**/*.groovy,resources/**`

# CIP validation gate

Applies whenever CIP artifacts are **created, modified, fixed, or declared complete**
(design path, bugfix path, or direct edits).

> **Iron Law (`verification-before-completion`):** NO completion claims without fresh
> verification evidence in the **same turn**.

## Scope — lint ALL changed CIP conf-model files

Run **`ReadLints`** on **every** changed file matching:

| Pattern | Artifact |
|---------|----------|
| `*.chain.cip.yaml` | Chain |
| `*.service.cip.yaml` | Integration service |
| `*.specification-group.cip.yaml` | Spec group |
| `*.specification.cip.yaml` | Spec version |
| `resources/*.groovy` | Scripts referenced by chains |

**Fail closed:** any schema linter **ERROR** on any file in scope ⇒ **not deployable**.

## Catalog hierarchy checks (specification files)

When a `*.specification.cip.yaml` is created or changed, verify in the same turn:

1. **`content.parentId`** is present and equals the parent **specification-group** `id`.
2. **`content.labels`** is present (use `[]` if empty).
3. Hierarchy is consistent:
   - `service` ← `specification-group.parentId`
   - `specification-group` ← `specification.parentId`
4. Prefer **`specificationSources`** + OpenAPI under `resources/source-…/` (repo convention);
   flag hand-authored `source: MANUAL` specs without a source file as **VALIDATION WARNING**.

Missing `parentId` is a **blocking** defect (schema-required).

## Sparse YAML checks (chain files)

When a `*.chain.cip.yaml` is created or changed by generators, flag:

1. **ERROR** — optional metadata emitted as `""`:
   `content.description`, `content.businessDescription`, `content.assumptions`,
   `content.outOfScope`
2. **WARNING** — `description: ""` on every element (omit key per CORPORATE_CIP_STANDARDS §2.4)
3. **ERROR** — quoted numeric properties where numbers are required (`retryCount: "3"`)
4. **WARNING** — unnecessary `chainId` on nested elements when export-profile is minimal

## Required before "done" / "complete" / "ready to deploy"

1. **`ReadLints`** on all files in scope — report per-file error/warning counts.
2. **`cip-chain-validator`** when compiler runtime is available. Verdict:
   **PASS** / **PASS-WITH-WARNINGS** / **FAIL**.
3. Summarize evidence using the **Completion template** below.

## Forbidden without attached evidence

- Phrases: "Design execution complete", "validation passed", "chain is valid/ready",
  "looks good", "should work"
- Hand-writing on the **design path**:
  - `*.chain.cip.yaml`
  - `*.service.cip.yaml`, `*.specification-group.cip.yaml`, `*.specification.cip.yaml`
  - Use **`cip-design-executor`** → **`cip-chain-assembler`** → **`cip-folder-organizer`**
    (see `cip-design-gate`). `cip-service-call-generator` **consumes** catalog IDs; it does
    not create spec files.
- Emitting optional chain metadata as empty strings (`""`) instead of omitting keys
- Declaring done after linting only the chain while companion service/spec files also changed
- Declaring done after only reading skills or copying patterns from other chains

## When full validator runtime is unavailable

Do **not** imply success. State explicitly:

> **VALIDATION INCOMPLETE** — `cip-chain-validator` runtime not executed (reason: …).
> Schema linter: \<per-file error counts\>.

Linter on **all** conf-model files in scope is the **minimum** bar, not a substitute for
`cip-chain-validator`.

## Completion template (mandatory for CIP integration work)

```
## Verification
- Chain: <path> — linter: <0 / N errors>
- Service: <path or n/a> — linter: <0 / N errors>
- Spec group: <path or n/a> — linter: <0 / N errors>
- Spec: <path or n/a> — linter: <0 / N errors>; parentId: <present → group id | MISSING>
- Scripts: <paths or n/a>
- Sparse YAML: <no empty optional metadata | list violations>
- cip-chain-validator: <PASS | FAIL | NOT RUN — reason>
- Deployable: <yes only if ALL linter 0 errors AND validator PASS/PASS-WITH-WARNINGS>
```

## Escalation

If linter errors remain after a fix attempt, stop claiming progress — list remaining
violations per file and fix or ask the user before continuing.

When editing any APM primitive (`apm.yml`, `*.instructions.md`, `SKILL.md`,
`*.prompt.md`, `*.agent.md`, hooks, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`),
apply the `apm-authoring` skill.

In a repo that uses APM, do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
or deployed skill files directly — they are regenerated by
`apm install` / `apm compile`. Edit the matching primitive under
`.apm/` and re-run `apm compile`.
